Chronic sleep deprivation has been linked to a host of health issues, including obesity, cardiovascular disease, and a weakened immune system. Furthermore, lack of sleep severely impairs cognitive functions such as attention, decision-making, and reaction times, increasing the risk of accidents. Adults generally require between seven and nine hours of sleep per night for optimal health, while children and teenagers need significantly more. Prioritizing good sleep hygiene, such as maintaining a consistent sleep schedule, is essential for overall well-being.
